entities.summary:
Boso was an Italian prelate and Cardinal of the Roman Catholic church, serving as Pope from 1180 until his death in 1181. 

He played a crucial role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire during this period, navigating complex relationships with European monarchs and the Church hierarchy.

One notable event that occurred during Boso's papacy was the Third Crusade, led by King Richard I of England, which sought to recapture Jerusalem from Muslim forces. 

Boso's legacy can be seen in the establishment of several monasteries and churches throughout Italy, which continue to hold significant cultural and historical value today.

The Italian city of Mantua, where Boso spent part of his life, remains a testament to his influence on local politics and architecture.
